t:
(a) Notwithstanding section 1356(n) of title 8, United States Code, of the funds deposited into the Immigration Examinations Fee Account, $7,500,000 shall be allocated by United States Citizenship and Immigration Services in fiscal year 2013 for the purpose of providing an immigrant integration grants program. 
    (b) For an additional amount for “United States Citizenship and Immigration Services” for the purpose of providing immigrant integration grants, $2,500,000. 
    (c) None of the funds made available to United States Citizenship and Immigration Services for grants for immigrant integration may be used to provide services to aliens who have not been lawfully admitted for permanent residence.

fable.w: The section only allocates and appropriates funds for an immigrant integration grants program and restricts how those funds may be used. The tempting reading is that a grants program brings outside organizations into contact with the agency, but receiving or applying for grants is not participation in a federal decision. Nothing here provides for consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or a right to sue.
fable.s: for the purpose of providing an immigrant integration grants program

opus.w: The section only allocates funds to a USCIS grants program and limits who can receive services funded by it. Grant programs and grant applications are expressly excluded from participation. Although grantees may be organizations outside the government, nothing here requires the government to consult them or let them shape a federal decision.
opus.s: $7,500,000 shall be allocated by United States Citizenship and Immigration Services in fiscal year 2013 for the purpose of providing an immigrant integration grants program.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that an "immigrant integration grants program" brings outside organizations into the government's work. That reading fails because the DEFINITION expressly excludes applications for benefits or grants. The section only allocates money and limits how it can be used. It requires no comment period, hearing, advisory body or consultation with outsiders before a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the allocation of funds for an immigrant integration grants program. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants' from the scope of participation. There is no requirement for consultation, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties in the decision-making process described here; it is purely an appropriation and funding directive.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds made available to United States Citizenship and Immigration Services for grants for immigrant integration may be used to provide services to aliens who have not been lawfully admitted for permanent residence.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for "grants," and grants often involve applications from outside entities, this constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." The section merely authorizes the allocation of funds for a grant program; it does not describe a process where outside parties consult with the government or participate in the decision-making process itself. The act of applying for a grant is not considered participation under this definition.
